idea-plugin.name: Test-Only Method Detector
idea-plugin.description:
Reports production Java methods whose every caller lives in a test source root — production API kept alive only by the tests that assert on it. Such a method inflates the public surface, blocks refactoring, and still counts as covered in coverage reports.

Why not just use Unused declaration?

IntelliJ can already compute this, via Unused declaration → Entry points → "When entry points are in test sources, mark callees as: unused". But that option works by stripping entry-point status from everything in a test source root, so your @Test methods are reported as unused too, with the identical "never used" message. The distinction is computed and then discarded. It is also a profile-wide setting shared with the on-the-fly unused-symbol inspection, so enabling it changes the daily editor experience.

This plugin reports the same finding as its own category, with its own severity and suppression id, leaving Unused declaration untouched.

What is excluded

  • Methods with no callers at all — that is plain dead code, and Unused declaration's job.
  • Framework entry points, resolved through the platform's own registered entry points and your Settings | Editor | Inspections | Entry points configuration — so Spring @Bean, @KafkaListener, @Scheduled and @EventListener methods, JPA no-arg constructors and Jackson accessors are left alone.
  • Constructors, main, record accessors, and methods overriding library declarations.
  • Methods carrying an annotation from an editable list, seeded with @TestOnly, both @VisibleForTesting variants, and generated-code markers (@Generated, @AvroGenerated). Add your own team's conventions, or remove entries to report annotated methods anyway.

Each finding is confirmed against the index before it is reported, so a reference from Spring XML, SpEL, a .properties file or javadoc suppresses it.

How to run it

  • Enable Method used only from test code in Settings | Editor | Inspections — it is off by default.
  • Run Analyze | Inspect Code with test sources included in the scope. Without them, a test-only method is indistinguishable from a fully dead one, and the inspection refuses to guess.
  • This is a global inspection: it runs only via Inspect Code and will never highlight as you type.

Source, documentation and a worked example of every case: GitHub. MIT licensed.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.0
  • Initial release.
  • Reports production Java methods whose every caller lives in a test source root.
  • Excludes framework entry points, constructors, main, record accessors and methods overriding library declarations.
  • Confirms each finding against the index, so references from Spring XML, SpEL, properties files and javadoc suppress the report.
  • Editable list of annotations that suppress reporting, on the method or its class. Seeded with @TestOnly and both @VisibleForTesting variants, plus generated-code markers (@Generated, @AvroGenerated).
